paper_metadata.title: Enhanced strength of L12-strengthened (FeCoNi)79.5Cr10.5Al5Ti5 high-entropy alloy via Ta alloying and its refined strengthening mechanism model

evidence.quote: In this study, we enhance the strength of L12-strengthened high-entropy alloy, proposed in our previous study, by Ta alloying.

TaHEA-HR displays a coarse yet strong FCC matrix generated by the hot-rolling process, with an average grain size and KAM value of ~88.4 μm and ~1.79°, respectively.
TaHEA-A700 exhibits slight grain growth of the FCC matrix (average grain size of ~99.3 μm) during the direct aging process but still shows a high average KAM value of ~1.61°.

Fig. 2(a) discovers that discontinuous precipitation (DP) occurs selectively at grain boundaries [26,27] and shows a very limited region fraction of 5.74%, which is reduced from that of HEA-A700 (8.05%) [17].
The phase fraction and mean radius of CP precipitates in TaHEA-A700 are 18.5% and 4.32 nm, respectively, both of which have increased compared to those in HEA-A700.

A high dislocation density of ~1.1 × 10^14 m^-2, calculated by CMWP method on the XRD line profile of TaHEA-A700, strongly supports that TaHEA-A700 has a coarse yet strong FCC matrix even after the aging process.
White coarse particles in Fig. 2(a) are characterized as Al-rich oxides, potentially originating from oxygen contamination during the alloy fabrication processes (Fig. S1) [17].
